newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Troops loot in Zairean diamond capital and flee.
newsitem.headline: Troops loot in Zairean diamond capital and flee.

text.p: Zairean soldiers looted vehicles and shops in Zaire's diamond mining capital Mbuji-Mayi on Friday and residents were afraid to leave their homes, sources in the town said.

Troops stole vehicles from the state-owned La Miniere de Bakwanga (MIBA) diamond mining company and looted diamond dealers' businesses before fleeing towards the town of Kananga, about 100 km (62 miles) to the west, expatriate sources said.

Businessmen in Lubumbashi who managed to speak to colleagues in Mbuji-Mayi by telephone on Friday afternoon said Zairean soldiers looted premises belonging to Lebanese diamond traders and had plundered stores selling electronic goods.
"They said there was still lots of shooting going on, and no one dares go out on the streets," one businessman told Reuters.

Rebels were believed to be in villages on the outskirts of Mbuji-Mayi in the diamond-rich East Kasai province, but there were no confirmed sightings of rebel fighters in the city itself, the sources said.
The diamond trade in Mbuji-Mayi deals mostly with industrial quality stones.
Zaire Airlines said it did not expect to stop in the city on its scheduled flight on the Lubumbashi-Kinshasa route on Saturday.

Sources from Zaire's Gecamines mining company in Lubumbashi said that a column of rebels took the town of Luena, 300 km (186 miles) northwest of Lubumbashi on Friday morning and were heading southwards.
There had been little if any fighting in Luena and youths in the area were rallying to the side of the rebels, who were apparently heading for Lubumbashi.
The MIBA mine, 20 percent owned by Belgium company Sibeka, produced around 6.5 million carats of diamonds in 1996.
